goal_title: Book: Procedural Generation: Rules Build Worlds — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in proceduralgeneration became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.
success_criteria: every open task here is done or skipped with a note
the chapters read through without a stumble in the headset
every code excerpt and number in the chapters matches the source

reading.arc: The sequence moves from selection to inhabitation. It opens by letting a score choose among described bodies and asking what that score cannot notice (a drawn torus the estimator never counts), then makes growth explicit as target assignment and summed unit directions (Space Colonization), narrows it to one nearest invitation and discovers that stored records and visible positions can diverge (Branching Growth), tests connection under a stated rule of contact (Percolation), asks a rule to carve room for a body (Caves / Mazes), samples and cuts material (Sculpted Forms), and closes by composing copying with connecting (Mirrored Patterns). The refrain throughout is that a record, a picture and a place to stand are three different relations that must each be built and checked; the museum's own floor, ramps and decks supply the support the generated things never do. Every hall is a six-button desk with a RULE card that reveals the operation only after the visitor has followed it, and every chapter asks for a prediction or a choice before the first press.
holds: The HOLD witness on a side plinth, inherited from LSystems_Living through Assemblage: Genetic, Space Colonization, Branching and Mirrored each keep an independent copy that survives RESET ('the held witness remains').

Predict before you press: choose a body and remember your reason; which way would you go; find the nearest point; where could something pass; look for the space that would have to remain empty; choose the moment the next construction inherits.
The six-button desk with RULE last: the operation is named only after it has been followed, and each chapter quotes one or two lines of the running source at the moment they matter.

Support versus generation: decks and ramps carry the visitor because the museum supplies collision; candidates, drawn branches, pink flowing sites, the sampled surface and the observation specimen do not. 'A connected parent record, a visible shape and a place you can inhabit are three relations we must learn to build together.'
Budgets are not maturity: 192 nodes / 60 generations, 192 records, 64 generations, 128 maze steps are named as what the program spends.
Each chapter ends by naming the next hall and the smaller difference to look for there, until the last one, which summarises the sequence without naming Soft Bodies.

hall_notes.note: Opens the sequence by asking the visitor to choose a body before the score does, then uses TARGET, RING, RULE and STEP to expose the seam between builder and evaluator: a torus is drawn but never counted, a box's volume is scale product times eight, overlaps are never subtracted. The best-argued chapter; its second paragraph is the one place it looks backward too far, and the raised deck it sends you to carries a screen it never mentions.

The construction chapter: three requests, unit vectors, a sum, one 0.5 m step, predicted before it is pressed, then FIELD (8 points, a 96-point sine-authored canopy) and POLICY (tips versus network). Reads as a careful demonstration whose numbers all hold; the first instruction names colours the hall does not draw that way.

Short and sharp: one nearest invitation, a predicted (-0.4, 0.3, 0), and the discovery that the readout's records and its distinct positions need not agree because an old site keeps re-choosing the same target. The sequence's best 'useful failure'; one code token leaks into the prose.

Face versus corner contact, the six-neighbour excerpt, LATTICE and DENSITY at 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.6 from one seed, and the collision distinction (white collides, pink does not). Tight and true; 'z face' is a code axis the visitor cannot see.

Two generators in one hall: carving centres with two cells of headroom versus backtracking that pops a stack. The stack excerpt lands well and the cave's authored bias is honestly named; the closing paragraph lets the author's desktop test harness into the reader's ear.

DROP, SAMPLE, VOXEL and ORIGINAL make 'what did the sample keep' concrete (centres, not rotations or contact shapes), and the dome's CUT shows absence as authored. Weak spots: the subtraction excerpt is the section view's cutter, not a core's, and 'repaired scene' is a process note.

Holding a field and stencilling it isolates copying from updating; NETWORK counts edges, components and cycles and refuses to let a skin certify a route. Ends with the sequence's summary sentence but names neither the desk's own word 'rhizome' nor the hall the thread goes to next.

stumbles: PG_Genetic_Evolution: the second paragraph stacks five back-references (rewriting a description, the cube family, altered amount / face selection, six kept results, the Form Finding height test) before the room's own idea; the visitor arriving from the textile hall must recall two halls back and eight sequences back.
PG_Genetic_Evolution: 'take the side ramp onto the raised structure' leads straight to a cased science screen (map row 22) that the chapter never places; a reader may take it for part of the lesson.
PG_Space_Colonization: 'The gold lines show those requests' — the threads to the points are drawn in muted mauve; the gold marks are the short unit-direction stubs and the chosen site.
PG_Space_Colonization: 'a restriction easy to miss in the name of this artifact' — the chapter never says the name.
PG_Branching_Growth: 'Keep the nearby organic_space in view' reads as a variable name.
PG_Percolation_Network: 'supplied from one z face' and 'the opposite face' — the visitor sees a 9 m cube with a source wall, not an axis.
PG_Caves_Mazes: 'The desktop check follows open maze cells from entrance to exit' — a headset visitor has no desktop check; this is the author's test record.
PG_Sculpted_Forms: the excerpt cut.operation = CSGShape3D.OPERATION_SUBTRACTION is introduced as the cores' operation but is the section view's extra cutter.
PG_Sculpted_Forms: 'Its repaired scene' — the reader never saw it broken.

PG_Mirrored_Patterns: the desk readout prints 'rhizome' while the chapter says 'the next policy'; and the closing paragraph carries 'the unresolved part into the next hall' without naming Soft Bodies, the only chapter in the sequence not to name its successor.

keep.quote: This is what fitness means in this room. We can inspect it without agreeing that it measures what we value.
Survival does not tell us that every surviving feature was rewarded.
A distant point will not get a longer vote merely because it is farther away.
A connected parent record, a visible shape and a place you can inhabit are three relations we must learn to build together.
The remainder is not always an extravagant shape. Sometimes it is redundant work concealed by a familiar outline.
The same event is connection for one system and a change of resistance for another.
A connected line has no width. Your shoulders do.
A hole can carry as much authorship as the material around it.

reading.handover_in: Strong. Assemblage_Same_Desire ends (line 52): 'Next, generated forms will be compared using a numerical score... What changes when a program is asked to decide which result should continue?' and PG_Genetic_Evolution opens by asking the visitor to choose a body and remember the reason before the score picks. The only friction is that Genetic's second paragraph reaches past Assemblage to the cube family (LSystems_Shape_Grammars, two halls back) and the Forge's height test (FormFinding_Forge, eight sequences back) without naming either hall; Shape Grammars line 61 had already made that bridge.
reading.handover_out: Soft. PG_Mirrored_Patterns closes with the sequence summary and 'carry the unresolved part into the next hall' but does not name Soft Bodies; SoftBodies_Soft_Body_Deformation opens on the jelly cube and reaches back to 'translation, rotation and scale' (line 17) rather than to anything in this sequence. The shared thread is present on both sides — positions moving while connectivity stays prescribed; collider, support and pinned points as the body's conditions — but neither chapter states it, so the reader crosses the seam unaccompanied for the first time in seven halls.

tasks.title: Turn the 'deliberately described here' aside into the number the reader needs
tasks.spec:
[prose] PG_Sculpted_Forms
Quote: “The extent is deliberately described here as the program computes it: `ceil(cube_size / voxel_size)` cells in each direction.”
Why: 'Deliberately described here' is the writer defending a choice to the reader and reads as a manual; what the reader needs is how far the mark reaches at the opening setting, which the sentence withholds.
Do: 'The program marks `ceil(cube_size / voxel_size)` cells in each direction around that address: two cells each way at the opening setting, a two-and-a-half-metre box around a one-metre cube.'
